article.articleHeadline: Lyme: la "enfermedad de los famosos" y una epidemia motorizada por el cambio climático
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Lyme disease: the 'disease of the famous' and an epidemic driven by climate change.
article.articleSummary: Lyme disease (borreliosis), caused by Borrelia burgdorferi and transmitted by Ixodes scapularis ticks, is the most common tick-borne illness in the United States and Europe and is expanding due to climate change. World Lyme Disease Day is observed on May 1. Originating from Old Lyme, Connecticut in the early 1970s, the disease cycles through deer, some mice and birds, with ticks acquiring the bacterium and biting humans. Warmer winters and longer, warmer springs enable ticks to thrive in forests, tall vegetation, and peri-urban parks and gardens. A 2022 BMJ Global Health study estimates about 14.5% of the world population (≈1.05 billion) infected at some point, highest in central Europe (21%), East Asia (16%), Western Europe (13.5%). Diagnosis begins with a small red bump and an expanding rash that clears in the center 3–30 days after a bite; three stages exist, with Stage 1 featuring fever, vomiting, malaise, neck stiffness and flu-like symptoms.

triage.headline_ja: ライム病：「著名人の病気」と気候変動によって推進されるパンデミック
triage.triage_reason: ライム病の世界的拡大と気候変動への関連性についての一般向け啓発記事。医学的には重要だが、急性的な新規アウトブレイク事象ではなく、確立した疾患の長期的な流行動向の解説が主体。
triage.notes: 記事の主題はライム病の世界的流行動向についての啓発記事。中国（東アジア）は統計データの対象に含まれているが、新規アウトブレイク事象ではなく、確立した疾患の拡大パターンについての一般情報。米国コネチカット州は対象国リストに含まれないため除外。東アジア（中国含む）でも16%の感染率が指摘されており、気候変動に伴う長期曝露リスクが増加する可能性がある。ただし、緊急対応が必要な新規事象ではなく、背景的な流行動向の解説。

article.articleHeadline: Kota Tanjungpinang Catat 55 Kasus Malaria Hingga April 2026, Senggarang dan Kampung Bugis Terbanyak - Kepri
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: City of Tanjungpinang records 55 malaria cases as of April 2026, Senggarang and Kampung Bugis have the most - Riau Islands
article.articleSummary: Malaria in Tanjungpinang, Riau Islands, reported 55 cases through April 2026, exceeding the total 53 cases recorded in 2025. The neighborhoods Senggarang and Kampung Bugis account for most infections. Officials note many cases are relapses or imported infections subsequently transmitted via Anopheles mosquitoes. The city’s swampy environment provides breeding sites for the malaria vector, contributing to elevated risk in Senggarang and Kampung Bugis. Health authorities urge heightened vigilance, environmental sanitation, and measures to prevent bites. Preventive actions include bed nets, insect repellent, and early medical checkups to curb transmission. Rustam, head of the Tanjungpinang Health Office, emphasizes the vulnerability of these areas due to abundant wetlands and mosquito habitats. The report highlights ongoing transmission dynamics and calls for continued surveillance and community preventive practices.

triage.headline_ja: タンジュンピナン市、2026年4月までにマラリア55例を記録、センガラン地区とカンプン・ブギス地区で最多 - リアウ諸島州
triage.triage_reason: インドネシアにおけるマラリア事例が2025年の年間53例を超える55例に達し、継続的な伝播リスクが示唆されているが、現時点では国際的拡大の兆候や深刻な公衆衛生被害の明確な証拠に欠ける。情報追加を待つ必要がある。
triage.notes: タンジュンピナン市のマラリア事例数が2025年の年間累計を上回る前年比増加傾向を示している。湿地帯の存在とハマダラカの生息環境が継続的なリスク要因となっている。WPROスクリーニング基準で異常性、長期曝露、流行しやすさの3つが該当するが、死亡例や重症例の報告がなく、情報が限定的であるためWATCHの判定とした。

article.articleHeadline: Đề xuất phạt tới 4 triệu đồng nếu để móng tay dài khi bán đồ ăn: 'Đây là ổ chứa vi khuẩn, dễ gây lây nhiễm sang thực phẩm'
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Proposal to fine up to 4 million dong if you have long nails when selling food: 'This is a breeding ground for bacteria, easily contaminating food'.
article.articleSummary: Vietnam's Ministry of Health is proposing to raise penalties to up to 4 million VND for food-safety violations as food poisoning cases rise. Experts say the measure would deter violations and raise compliance across food businesses. Violations cited include selling food on unsanitary surfaces, in areas infested by insects, or having direct handlers who do not wear masks, trim nails, or use gloves when processing ready-to-eat foods. Long nails are described as potential reservoirs for pathogens such as Salmonella, Escherichia coli O157, and Norovirus, which can contaminate food through contaminated hands. Handwashing, per WHO guidance, can reduce up to 44% of gastrointestinal and respiratory infections. Enforcement remains challenging due to many outlets, so officials call for intersectoral coordination, intensified inspections, and public awareness campaigns while the draft administrative penalties decree on food safety is reviewed by authorities.

triage.headline_ja: 食品販売時の長い爪に対し最大400万ドンの罰金提案：『これは細菌の温床であり、食品への感染を招きやすい』
triage.triage_reason: ベトナムにおける食品由来感染症（ノロウイルス、腸チフス、パラチフス、大腸菌）に関連する公衆衛生対策の提案。複数の病原体が関連し規制強化が進行中だが、現在のところ特定の流行発生は記事に記載されておらず、政策提案段階であるため情報が限定的。
triage.notes: 記事は食品安全規制の強化提案が主題であり、現在の流行発生ではなく政策対応段階。ただし、ノロウイルス、腸チフス、パラチフス、大腸菌O157など複数の食品由来病原体が言及されており、食品汚染リスクが認識されている。ベトナム保健省による規制強化の動きは進行中であり、経過観察が適切。

article.articleHeadline: Bird flu scare in Maharashtra: 1.4 lakh chickens to be culled in Nandurbar
article.articleSummary: Bird flu avian influenza outbreak in Navapur, Navapur taluka, Nandurbar district, Maharashtra. After 150–200 chickens died at a poultry farm on April 13–14, samples tested positive for avian influenza at a government lab. Authorities ordered culling of about 1.4 lakh chickens within a one-km containment zone around infected farms; around six farms fall inside. A three-km surveillance/containment zone and a five-km buffer were also established. Transport and sale of poultry products from the area were restricted. A district-level committee was formed to inspect farms across Navapur taluka; enhanced monitoring at poultry markets and transport points followed. This is the third bird flu incident in Navapur, causing financial losses; the government will provide financial assistance under official rules. No human infections reported so far; officials urge caution and hygiene and reporting of unusual bird deaths.

triage.headline_ja: マハラシュトラ州の鳥インフルエンザ恐れ：ナンドゥルバルで14万羽の鶏が処分される予定

triage.notes: マハラシュトラ州ナンドゥルバル地区のナワプル村における動物での鳥インフルエンザ確定事例。既に地区レベルの対応委員会が設置され、処分・監視体制が構築されている。現在までのところ人間感染は報告されていないが、鳥インフルエンザの人獣共通感染のリスク考慮および今後の感染動向の監視が必要。

article.articleHeadline: Khởi tố vụ án giết mổ, tiêu thụ lợn nhiễm dịch tả châu Phi
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Indictment in the case of slaughtering and consuming African swine fever-infected pigs.
article.articleSummary: Indictment issued in Thanh Hóa Province, Vietnam, for slaughtering and consuming African swine fever (ASF)–infected pigs. On 31 March 2026, police at Hoằng Lộc checked a pig-slaughter facility owned by Nguyễn Văn Chiến and found 3 slaughtered pigs (total weight 384.5 kg) and 8 healthy-looking pigs in pens with disease signs. Chiến admitted ordering slaughter to sell the meat. He, along with Lê Văn Trung and Nguyễn Khắc Nguyên, were indicted. Trung had purchased 8 diseased pigs at a low price to resell, sourcing them from Nguyên, a farmer in Hiền Thôn, Hoằng Hóa, who detected illness but did not report it. Laboratory tests by the National Centre for Veterinary Diagnostics I confirmed ASF virus in meat and blood samples. Authorities seized 384.5 kg of pork and culled the 8 infected pigs; investigation remains ongoing as of 1 May 2026.

triage.headline_ja: アフリカ豚熱感染豚の屠殺・販売に関する刑事告発

triage.notes: アフリカ豚熱は家畜疾病であり、直接的なヒト健康への深刻な影響は記載されていない。ただし違法な屠殺・販売行為により感染拡大のリスクがあり、地域の疾病管理体制の脆弱性を示唆。WPRO基準では異常性と流行しやすさで該当するため要経過観察。

article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Squirrel Attacks Psychology Students — A Rodent Terrorizes the University in India.
article.articleSummary: As of May 1, 2026, a red palm squirrel attacked 20 people at Mohanlal Sukhadia University in Udaipur, Rajasthan, India, including the dean, mainly along the psychology faculty route. University investigators suspect the squirrel has nested near the campus and defends its territory aggressively. Potential factors include partial blindness, color-triggered reactions, or perceived threats from passersby. Rescue teams twice attempted to trap the animal, but it evaded capture. Authorities placed cages elsewhere and urged immediate reporting of sightings. Veterinary authorities from the Department of Livestock reassure that bites from palm squirrels do not carry rabies risk but stress the importance of tetanus vaccination. The species is identified as a reddish palm squirrel, native to India and Sri Lanka; the incident has disrupted student commuting and campus life.

article.articleHeadline: Karnataka: H5N1 confirmed in death of 44 peacocks in Tumakuru
article.articleSummary: H5N1 bird flu confirmed as cause of death for 44 peacocks in Tumakuru district, Karnataka, with initial reports on April 16. Lab analysis at the ICAR-National Institute of High Security Animal Diseases in Bhopal confirmed H5N1. No fresh deaths have been reported in Tumakuru taluk since April 23. A 10-km containment zone has been declared around the affected Kesaramadu, Hirehalli and Gulur gram panchayats; all poultry farms within the zone were alerted. Forest, Health, and Animal Husbandry/Veterinary Services authorities are coordinating containment efforts. Health facilities have been instructed to maintain surveillance for influenza-like illness and severe acute respiratory infection (ILI/SARI) and to keep adequate stocks of PPE, triple-layer masks, oseltamivir, viral transport medium, and throat swab kits. Ongoing monitoring and reporting as of May 1, 2026.

triage.headline_ja: カルナタカ州：トゥムクルでH5N1が44羽の孔雀の死亡原因として確認
triage.triage_reason: H5N1鳥インフルエンザの動物への感染確認で異常・予想外であり、人への感染リスク評価のため健康監視体制が構築されている。IHR基準（異常性、重症度）とWPRO基準（異常性、流行リスク、長期曝露）に複数該当。
triage.notes: H5N1確認は動物での発生（44羽の孔雀）だが、公式な健康監視体制（ILI/SARI監視、PPE・抗ウイルス薬の備蓄）が構築されており、人への感染リスク評価が行われている。10km隔離帯設置と複数省庁による統合対応が実施中。動物での確認が人での流行の可能性を示唆。

article.articleHeadline: Alagoas tem alta nas mortes por Influenza em 2026, com número cinco vezes maior que em 2025
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Alagoas records a rise in influenza deaths in 2026, five times higher than in 2025.
article.articleSummary: Six influenza deaths were recorded in Alagoas in the first four months of 2026, a fivefold increase from the same period in 2025. The first fatality was a 2-year-old boy in São Sebastião, Agreste; the second was a 7-year-old boy in Arapiraca, Agreste. In April, four more deaths occurred in Maceió, Marechal Deodoro, Joaquim Gomes, and Palmeira dos Índios; all victims were over 70 years old. One suspected case remains under investigation in Maceió (April). The influenza vaccination campaign runs through May 30, focusing on vulnerable groups, with vaccines available at health posts and fixed sites, including shopping centers and extended hours at health units. In Maceió, vaccination is offered at all health units, and 24 "Corujão da Saúde" units stay open until 9 p.m. The disease is an acute, vaccine-preventable respiratory infection with high transmission.

triage.headline_ja: アラゴアス州、2026年のインフルエンザ死亡者数が増加、2025年同期比5倍に
triage.triage_reason: ブラジル・アラゴアス州でインフルエンザによる死亡者が急増（5倍）しており、異常な増加パターンとして認識される。死亡例の報告と公衆衛生上の対応が実施されている点から、IHR基準の「異常性」「重症度」が該当し、フルRRA評価が必要。
triage.notes: 記事はブラジルのアラゴアス州および関連地域でのインフルエンザ死亡者の急増を報告している。死亡者数が5倍に増加し、小児（2歳、7歳）および高齢者（70歳以上）が被害を受けている。ワクチン接種キャンペーンが実施中であり、保健当局が対応している。ブラジルは対象国リストに含まれるため verified_locations に含める。

article.articleHeadline: Delhi govt set to declare leprosy a notifiable disease
article.articleSummary: Delhi will declare leprosy a notifiable disease under the Delhi Epidemic Diseases Act to strengthen surveillance, enable early detection and improve treatment adherence in the national capital. The proposal, cleared by the Delhi Health Department, awaits approval; once notified, hospitals, clinics and practitioners must report cases to the District Leprosy Officer for targeted interventions and timely diagnosis, with free Multi-Drug Therapy at government facilities. Delhi joins Tamil Nadu, Maharashtra, Karnataka, Uttarakhand and West Bengal in mandating notification. Health Minister Dr Pankaj Kumar Singh said the move will help identify hidden cases, curb transmission and ensure standard treatment with dignity. Notification is expected after approval under the Government of NCT of Delhi Act, 1991, with reporting guidelines to follow. India eliminated leprosy as a public-health problem in 2005, but accounts for about 59% of global new cases; around 44.1% are treated in private facilities and unreported, underscoring the need for mandatory notification per WHO guidance to strengthen surveillance, contact tracing and post-exposure prophylaxis.

triage.headline_ja: デリー政府がハンセン病を届出対象疾病に指定する方針
triage.triage_reason: ハンセン病は既に克服された疾患であり、本イベントは公衆衛生上の緊急事態ではなく、行政的な届出制度化である。ただしインドは世界全体の約59%の新規患者を占めており、疫学監視強化の必要性がある点で留意対象。
triage.notes: 本イベントはハンセン病の新規集団発生ではなく、インド政府による疾病届出制度の制度化である。インドは2005年にハンセン病を公衆衛生上の問題として克服しているが、世界全体の新規患者の約59%を占めており、特に民間医療機関での治療例（44.1%）が未報告となっていることが背景。WHO指針に基づく疫学監視強化の取り組みであり、現時点では WATCH レベル（要経過観察）として扱うが、実運用後の届出状況や対策の実効性について注視が必要。

article.articleHeadline: Demam Bukan Sekadar Gejala Biasa, Ini Pentingnya Deteksi Dini Infeksi
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Fever Is More Than Just a Common Symptom: The Importance of Early Detection of Infection
article.articleSummary: Fever, often deemed mild, is an early signal of infection rather than a trivial symptom. Without objective parameters to gauge severity, people risk delaying care and resorting to irrational self-medication with antibiotics. In Kabupaten Tangerang, high numbers of infection cases with suspected status underscore the need for systematic early detection at the community level. In response, health-tech innovations are being developed, including non-invasive wearable devices for real-time monitoring. The Smart Febrile Patch is a sweat-based sensor designed to help community screening of fever-related infections. It tracks three biomarkers: body temperature, sweat pH, and lactate levels—markers linked to inflammatory response, physiological stability, and early signs of tissue hypoperfusion. This approach offers a more comprehensive picture than temperature alone, enabling earlier identification of potential deterioration and guiding timely medical evaluation.

triage.headline_ja: 熱は単なる一般的な症状ではない：感染症の早期発見の重要性
triage.triage_reason: 記事は感染症の早期発見の重要性に関する教育的・啓発的コンテンツであり、具体的な感染症アウトブレイク、異常増加、または公衆衛生危機を報告していない。タンゲラン県での「疑い症例の多数」は記述的であり、具体的な症例数、死亡率、またはアウトブレイクの根拠を示していない。
triage.notes: 本記事は特定の感染症アウトブレイクを報告するものではなく、感染症検査の重要性に関するヘルスケア技術のプロモーション記事である。疾患名が『Unknown Illness』と記載されているが、サマリーの内容は一般的な感染症スクリーニング技術の紹介に過ぎない。IHR/WPROのいかなるシグナル基準も満たさない。

article.articleHeadline: Heatwave triggers rise in water-borne diseases across Hyderabad
article.articleSummary: Heatwave in Hyderabad exceeds 41°C for over a week, triggering a surge in water-borne diseases and kidney-related infections. Hospitals across Hyderabad and surrounding districts—Sangareddy, Vikarabad, Rangareddy, Medchal-Malkajgiri, Bhongir—report increased gastro cases, typhoid, and diarrhoea, along with heat-related illnesses. Doctors warn that contaminated water, street-side beverages, and ice from informal sectors fuel transmission, while dehydration and electrolyte loss heighten risk of Acute Kidney Injury (AKI). Private clinics, Fever Hospital Nallakunta, and Care Hospitals Malakpet note rising heat-induced nephropathy and renal strain due to dehydration and GI infections. Symptoms include fever, gastroenteritis, diarrhoea, and typhoid-like illness; emphasis on drinking treated water and hygienic food to prevent illness during summer.

triage.headline_ja: 熱波がハイデラバード全域の水系感染症の増加を引き起こす
triage.triage_reason: IHR基準3項目該当（異常性、国内複数地域での感染増加、公衆衛生への中程度の影響）およびWPRO基準複数該当。熱波によるインフラ脆弱化が背景にあり、水系感染症の多地域同時発生は国内の事前対応が必要。
triage.notes: 記事はハイデラバードおよびテランガナ州内の複数地域（Sangareddy, Vikarabad, Rangareddy, Bhongir等）での水系感染症の急増を報告。熱波（41°C超）が環境衛生悪化を加速し、非正規セクター由来の汚染水の使用が感染増大の主要因。複数の医療機関で患者数増加が確認されており、地域保健当局の関心が高い。国際的拡大リスクは低いが、国内における急速な事前対応が必要と判断される。

article.articleHeadline: Bird Flu Outbreak In Maharashtra: 1.4 Lakh Poultry Set To Be Culled In Navapur
article.articleSummary: Bird Flu (Avian Influenza) outbreak in Navapur, Maharashtra's Nandurbar district near the Gujarat border. Samples from Diamond Poultry Farm, Taslim Poultry Farm, and Don Poultry Farm tested positive for avian influenza at the National Institute of High Security Animal Diseases in Bhopal. About 1.4 lakh birds will be culled; culling and disposal of poultry, feed, and eggs within a 1-km radius of the affected zone, with a 1–10 km surveillance zone declared. Transportation, purchase, sale, and marketing of poultry banned in the affected areas. Rapid Response Teams deployed; sanitisation and disinfection operations ongoing. Measures follow the central action plan; Navapur has experienced prior outbreaks. Culling started on Friday, 2026-05-01.

triage.headline_ja: マハラシュトラ州の鳥インフルエンザ流行：ナヴァプルで1.4万羽の家禽が処分予定
triage.triage_reason: 鳥インフルエンザの動物での発生であり、異常かつ重症度は中程度以上（1.4万羽の処分規模）。ただし、記事サマリーはヒト感染の具体的証拠を示さず、動物疾病対応であるため、IHR基準2以上への該当判定は慎重に。スクリーニング基準複数該当するが、ヒト伝播リスク等の詳細情報不足。
triage.notes: 記事見出しに「Human Infection with Avian Influenza」が含まれているが、サマリー本文ではヒト感染の明示的な報告がなく、動物疾病対応に焦点が当たっている。マハラシュトラ州ナヴァプルの複数の養鶏場でH5N1の可能性が高い。過去の流行歴あり、地域的な対応体制は確立されている模様。ヒト感染リスクの有無を確認する続報が重要。

article.articleHeadline: 19:18:17衞生防護中心：增一宗外地傳入登革熱個案 700人接受健康評估無出現病徵
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: 19:18:17 Centre for Health Protection: One more imported dengue fever case; 700 people underwent health assessments with no symptoms observed.
article.articleSummary: Dengue fever and chikungunya updates from Hong Kong (published 2026-05-01). Dengue: one additional imported case reported; the patient had Vietnam exposure during incubation (Apr 24–30). A prior local dengue case prompted health assessments for about 700 people at the same site; all remained asymptomatic, with no epidemiological link found. Hong Kong’s 2026 dengue tally stands at 17 (16 imported, 1 local); 2025 had 59 imported cases and 2024 had 161 (156 imported, 5 local). Globally, dengue remains high, with WHO recording over 14 million cases in 2024 and, Jan–Jul last year, over 4 million cases and more than 3,000 deaths across 97 countries. Nearby destinations report large counts (Indonesia, India, Vietnam >120,000 each; Malaysia/Thailand >50,000; Singapore >4,000). Guangdong Province (as of Apr 19) reported 69 dengue cases this year, 4 local. Chikungunya: no new locally transmitted Hong Kong cases Apr 24–30; year-to-date total remains 2 imported cases. Globally, 2025 up to Dec 10: 502,264 chikungunya cases and 186 deaths; Guangdong notes 3 cases this year (1 local) as of Apr 19.

triage.headline_ja: 衛生防護中心：輸入登革熱患者が1例増加、700人が健康評価を受けたが症状は見られない
triage.triage_reason: デング熱とチクングニアの複合信号であり、香港での輸入症例報告に加え、周辺国（ベトナム、インドネシア、マレーシア、タイなど）での大規模流行が背景にある。WHO基準では国際的蔓延リスクがあり、スクリーニング基準では異常性・流行性が該当し、公開情報源による報告であり、フルRRA実施が必要。
triage.notes: 香港（中国に含める）でのデング熱・チクングニアの輸入症例報告。東南アジア・南アジア地域で大規模流行中（2024年グローバル1,400万件超、2025年チクングニア50万件超）。輸入症例の発生源地域（ベトナム、インドネシア、インド、マレーシア、タイ）を verified_locations に含めた。公衆衛生当局による公式発表であり、情報の信頼性は高い。

article.articleHeadline: Bahaya Perdagangan Satwa Liar Ilegal Ancaman Zoonosis dan Pandemi Baru
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: The Dangers of Illegal Wildlife Trade: The Threat of Zoonosis and a New Pandemic
article.articleSummary: Illegal wildlife trade in Indonesia poses a serious global public-health threat by enabling zoonotic spillovers. IPB University ecogenetics expert Prof Ronny Rachman Noor warns that mammals entering global trade have about 1.5 times higher risk of hosting zoonotic pathogens than wildlife in the wild, driven by stress during capture and transport that weakens immunity. Citing a study from the University of Fribourg, the article notes that the historical link between human–wildlife contact and pandemics like SARS, MERS, and COVID-19 underscores current risks as illegal trade expands via social media and international distribution chains. A 2022 West Sumatra case involving illegal trade of king cockatoo, orangutan, and golden cat illustrates potential pathogen spillover. Biodiversity conservation and habitat protection are framed as essential public-health measures to prevent future crises; calls for strengthened surveillance and enforcement.

triage.headline_ja: 違法野生動物取引の危険性：人獣共通感染症とパンデミックの新たな脅威
triage.triage_reason: 違法野生動物取引によるズーノーシス伝播のリスク警告であり、WPROスクリーニング基準（異常性・長期曝露・流行しやすさ）に該当する可能性があるが、具体的な現在のアウトブレイク発生を示さず情報が限定的である。
triage.notes: 記事は警告・解説記事であり、進行中のアウトブレイクではなく潜在的リスク分析が主体。2022年西スマトラの事例言及にとどまる。インドネシアでの違法野生動物取引を主題として検証。WPROスクリーニング基準3項目該当（異常性、長期曝露リスク、流行しやすさ）だが、公衆衛生上の即座の影響の証拠がないため、継続的な監視が適切。

article.articleHeadline: Gia Lai ghi nhận ca mắc "vi khuẩn ăn thịt người" đầu tiên năm 2026
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Gia Lai records the first case of flesh-eating bacteria in 2026.
article.articleSummary: First Whitmore (melioidosis) case in Gia Lai province in 2026 due to Burkholderia pseudomallei. Patient K.H., a farmer from Mook Trang village, Ia Dom commune, Gia Lai, presented with fever, generalized pain, and poor appetite; admitted 19 April in severe condition with unconsciousness, sweating, and tachypnea. Laboratory confirmation identified Burkholderia pseudomallei. The patient has diabetes, a risk factor for severe disease, and is being weaned from mechanical ventilation with ICU monitoring. This marks Gia Lai’s initial Whitmore case for 2026, with epidemiology linking exposure to soil, mud, and natural water during farming; no additional local cases detected to date. Public health actions include 14-day contact monitoring and intensified health messaging. Preventive guidance emphasizes protective gear for workers, avoiding polluted water, covering wounds, and seeking medical care for suspected infection, given Whitmore’s potential severity and high mortality if untreated.

triage.headline_ja: ジア・ライ省が2026年初のライム病（メリオイドーシス）患者を記録
triage.triage_reason: ベトナムでメリオイドーシス（Burkholderia pseudomallei感染）の初症例が確認され、重症化（ICU入院、人工呼吸器使用）している。地域で異常な発生であり、適切な対応体制と疫学調査が進行中。
triage.notes: ジア・ライ省での初症例であるが、患者は重症化（意識消失、人工呼吸器装着）しており、死亡リスクが高い。環境曝露（土壌、泥、自然水）が原因で、農業従事者におけるリスク継続の可能性がある。糖尿病を基礎疾患に持つため、重症化の危険因子が存在。接触者の14日間監視と公衆衛生メッセージが実施中で、管理可能性は保たれている。

article.articleHeadline: Dinkes Tanjungpinang: Kasus malaria meningkat tiga tahun terakhir
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Tanjungpinang Health Office: Malaria Cases Have Increased Over the Past Three Years
article.articleSummary: Malaria in Tanjungpinang, Kepulauan Riau, Indonesia, has risen over three years after elimination in 2014. Dinkes Tanjungpinang reports 129 cases in 2024, 59 in 2025, and 29 by April 2026. Of 18 kelurahan, Kampung Bugis and Senggarang are highest risk, with dense Anopheles vectors and environmental factors such as saltwater ponds conducive to transmission. Human mobility, including workers from malaria-endemic areas, also contributes to spread. Preventive measures include larval control with fish predation in ponds, use of larvicides, and migrant health surveillance. Diagnosis and treatment are prioritized to prevent further spread. Residents should seek care at puskesmas or hospitals if malaria symptoms appear (1–2 hour chills, fever, sweating, severe headache) to ensure prompt treatment and control.

triage.headline_ja: タンジュンピナン保健局：マラリア症例が過去3年間で増加
triage.triage_reason: インドネシアにおけるマラリアの再出現で異常・予想外性がありスクリーニング基準を満たすが、症例数は比較的限定的であり、国際的拡大リスクや重症度の詳細が不明確なため。情報収集を継続すべき段階。
triage.notes: インドネシア・タンジュンピナン地域でマラリアが2014年の排除後に再出現。2024年129例、2025年59例、2026年4月までに29例と報告されている。ベクターと環境要因が確認されており、労働者による移入が要因と考えられている。死亡例や重症例の記載がないため重症度は不明。地域的な対策が進行中。

article.articleHeadline: Svinjetina iz ove zemlje obara rekorde: Profitirali od afričke kuge u Evropi, prete da "pregaze" SAD
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Pork from this country is breaking records: Profited from African swine fever in Europe, threatening to crush the USA.
article.articleSummary: African swine fever (ASF) outbreaks in Europe, notably Spain’s wild boar, are reshaping pork markets. Rabobank notes indirect effects from geopolitical tensions and supply-chain disruptions, with transport costs rising due to potential strains like the Strait of Hormuz. Brazil emerges as the major beneficiary, exporting a record 381,000 tonnes of pork in Q1 2026. Japan’s imports from Brazil surged 60% to 43,000 tonnes, while the Philippines remained the largest Brazil market at 121,000 tonnes. U.S. pork exports to Japan rose 21% year over year, linked to Europe’s ASF disruptions that redirected demand. Spain halted exports to Japan in late 2025, but early 2026 shipments continued under prior approvals, with inventories expected to dwindle in Q2. Overall, ASF and logistics are pressuring European producers while boosting Brazil’s export position.

triage.headline_ja: この国の豚肉が記録を更新：ヨーロッパでのアフリカ豚熱から利益を得、米国を「圧倒する」と脅す
triage.triage_reason: 本イベントはアフリカ豚熱（ASF）の市場経済影響に関する報道であり、現在の疫学的な発生状況の新たな報告ではない。公衆衛生への直接的な懸念、ヒト感染リスク、または国際的に管理されていない拡大の可能性がなく、IHR基準およびWPRO基準の該当が限定的である。
triage.notes: 本記事は既知のASF発生（ヨーロッパ、スペイン）に関連する商業的・経済的影響に焦点を当てたものである。新たな疾病発生の報告ではなく、市場再編成と貿易フロー変化についての分析記事と考えられる。ASFが家畜に限定された動物疾病であり、ヒト感染の懸念はないため、IHR基準は満たさない。対象国はBrazilとPhilippinesのみであり、これらは主に市場としての言及である。

article.articleHeadline: 潮興撈海鮮暗藏致盲危機　新型病毒直接傳人
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Chao Xing seafood harvesters hide a risk of blindness; a novel virus directly transmits to humans.
article.articleSummary: A novel virus, referred to in Chinese as 偷死野田村病毒, detected in aquaculture ponds, can directly infect humans and is linked to eye disease. As of May 1, 2026, mainland China reports dozens of eye illnesses plausibly connected to this virus, with severe cases manifesting uveitis, eye pain, blurred vision, photophobia, and raised intraocular pressure, risking blindness. The virus historically circulates among pond-raised shrimp and fish; human infection is suspected after handling seafood or consuming raw/undercooked products, though the exact transmission mechanism remains unclear. Hong Kong seafood harvesters who travel inland to collect seafood are noted as at risk. Public health guidance emphasizes wound disinfection, tetanus vaccination if not up to date, and prompt medical care; saline irrigation is advised for ocular exposure. Additional cautions include cooking seafood thoroughly and avoiding potential bacterial infections from wounds during handling.

triage.headline_ja: 潮興撈海鮮暗藏致盲危機　新型病毒直接傳人
triage.triage_reason: 新規病原体による眼疾患の流行（複数の重症例）が報告されており、ヒト-ヒト感染の可能性、国際的拡大リスク（香港との関連）、および管理可能性の懸念が認められるため、IHR基準2つ以上かつWPRO基準複数該当でシグナルとして識別。
triage.notes: 記事は香港の海産物採集者による中国本土への移動に言及しているが、実際の流行報告は中国本土（複数の眼疾患例）が主体。香港は地理的リスク地域として言及されるが、発症例の主な報告地は中国本土。新規病原体による重症眼疾患（失明リスク）の流行、ヒト-ヒト感染の可能性、水産物経由の感染ルートが指摘されている。疾患名フィールドに「Tetanus」と記載されているが、サマリーの内容（新規病毒、眼疾患、uveitis等）と不整合があり、情報提供者による分類エラーの可能性がある。

article.articleHeadline: Early In A Pandemic, Some Hosts Might Act As "Evolutionary Accelerators" For The Virus
article.articleSummary: University of Utah researchers show host genetics and sex can drive influenza virus evolution, potentially creating 'evolutionary accelerators' that could worsen outbreaks. In an H3N2 influenza A model adapted to mice, the virus evolved into 28 lineages over 10 replication cycles in two mouse strains; infections in female mice of one strain yielded more virulent mutations, while another strain showed fewer overall, indicating host sex and genotype can shape virulence trajectories. Three-dimensional mapping tracked viral protein sites under selection. Although results are in mice, they suggest that if humans display similar dynamics, early infections could seed more virulent strains. Implications include prioritizing vaccination for groups likely to select for virulence first. Context references historical pandemics such as the Hong Kong flu (1968–1970) and the 1918–19 pandemic, and notes H5N1 multi-species outbreaks.

triage.triage_reason: ユタ大学の研究に基づくインフルエンザウイルス進化に関する学術的分析であり、現在進行中の感染症アウトブレイク情報ではなく、実験室モデル研究から得られた理論的知見。記事サマリーには実際の患者発症や地域での流行拡大の報告がないため、シグナル評価は保留が適切。

article.articleHeadline: Delhi govt set to declare leprosy a notifiable disease
article.articleSummary: Delhi government plans to declare leprosy a notifiable disease under the Delhi Epidemic Diseases Act, mandating reporting by hospitals, clinics and practitioners to the District Leprosy Officer. Once notified, cases will be reported enabling targeted interventions, timely diagnosis and free MDT at government facilities, improving treatment adherence. The proposal, cleared by the Delhi Health Department, awaits approval under the GNCTD Act, 1991, with reporting guidelines to be issued soon. Delhi would join Tamil Nadu, Maharashtra, Karnataka, Uttarakhand and West Bengal in mandating notification. Health Minister Dr Pankaj Kumar Singh said the move will identify hidden cases, curb transmission and ensure standard treatment with dignity. India eliminated leprosy as a public health problem in 2005 but accounts for nearly 59% of global annual new cases; a pan-India study found 44.1% treated in private facilities go unreported, underscoring the need for mandatory notification per WHO guidance.

article.articleHeadline: Faster and Easier Ways to Diagnose Monkeypox: New Approaches Improve Detection
article.articleSummary: Mpox (monkeypox) diagnosis is shifting from PCR-only to accessible point-of-care tools. The WHO declared Public Health Emergency of International Concern for mpox in June 2022 and again in August 2024 as cases rose worldwide, with more than 60,000 cases in 100+ countries. PCR from skin lesions remains the gold standard but requires specialized labs and trained staff, limiting use at the point of care. A 2025 Trends in Biotechnology review surveys point-of-care platforms, immunological tests, isothermal amplification (LAMP/RPA), and CRISPR/Cas diagnostics, noting barriers such as cost, cold-chain needs, and limited multiplexing. Immunoassays (ELISA) have limited clinical utility; rapid antigen tests are faster (10–15 minutes) but less sensitive. Mpox first emerged in 1970 in the Democratic Republic of Congo with animal reservoirs and zoonotic transmission; symptoms include fever, myalgia, headache, lymphadenopathy, and vesiculopustular rash. Future directions include electrochemical and paper-based sensors, microfluidics, 3D printing, smartphones, and AI-driven lesion-image analysis within REASSURED.

article.articleHeadline: Envu India Supports National Conclave Uniting India's Public Health Leadership to  Advance Urban Vector-Borne Disease Control
article.articleSummary: Ahmedabad, Gujarat, India hosted a national technical conclave on urban pest management and vector control, concluded on 28 April 2026 after two days, organized by ISMOCD with Ahmedabad Municipal Corporation and supported by Envu India. Attended by senior public health leaders, government officials, Armed Forces Medical College, academic institutions, and international contributors, the meeting focused on dengue, malaria, and chikungunya in India’s expanding cities, advocating evidence-based, integrated vector management (IVM) beyond adulticidal fogging. Highlights included ovitrap-based surveillance with AI analysis, WHO-aligned IVM frameworks, Urban Malaria Scheme, National Urban Health Mission, mass-gathering preparedness, and innovations in public health insecticides. Envu shared Malaysia’s Integrated Dengue Epidemiology and Management (iDEM) insights. Background data cited: malaria deaths fell from ~800,000 at independence to 83 in 2023; kala-azar cases declined from 9,241 in 2014 to 449 in 2024; over 100 districts have eliminated lymphatic filariasis; dengue mortality also decreased. India aims to eliminate malaria, lymphatic filariasis, and kala-azar by 2030, underscoring academia–government–industry collaboration and safer, water-based vector-control formulations.

article.articleHeadline: Ученые выявили более 20 новых вирусов, способных заражать человека
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Scientists have identified more than 20 new viruses capable of infecting humans.
article.articleSummary: An updated ICTV catalog shows 239 RNA-containing viruses capable of infecting humans by end-2024 (including influenza, hepatitis, and coronaviruses). The taxonomy list, recognizing all ICTV taxa, adds 25 viruses since the previous edition, with over 20 new species identified in recent years. Most of these viruses are of animal origin; about 62% are zoonotic and do not spread between humans. Nevertheless, 60 viruses can epidemically affect or persist in humans. A distinct group comprises 32 human-to-human-transmissible viruses currently causing limited outbreaks, illustrating a spectrum of epidemic potential from strictly zoonotic to large-scale outbreaks. Vector-borne transmission accounts for about 43% of viruses, primarily via mosquitoes and ticks; many viruses have multiple routes, including airborne droplets, contact, and bodily fluids. Geography of detections: Americas 99, Eurasia 81, Africa/Middle East 43, Oceania 16. Since the early 20th century, RNA virus counts rose from 178 to 239, with 61 added in the 21st century.

article.articleHeadline: H5N1 bird flu confirmed in 44 peacock deaths in Karnataka's Tumakuru - CNBC TV18
article.articleSummary: Laboratory tests confirmed H5N1 avian influenza caused the deaths of 44 peacocks in Karnataka's Tumakuru district. Deaths occurred across Kesaramadu, Hirehalli and Gulur gram panchayats after first reporting on 16 April; samples sent to ICAR-NIHSAD in Bhopal confirmed the virus. No new deaths since 23 April, but containment measures remain. A 10-km containment zone is in place; all poultry farms within the radius have been alerted. Health authorities are increasing surveillance for Influenza-Like Illness (ILI) and Severe Acute Respiratory Infection (SARI) and ensuring stocks of PPE kits, masks, oseltamivir, viral transport medium, and throat swab kits. Karnataka conducted a 10-day intensive surveillance and containment drive following an outbreak detected on 14 April at Mathkuru in Hesaraghatta. Wildlife, health, and veterinary departments are coordinating to contain spread; no confirmed human cases reported as of 1 May 2026.

article.articleHeadline: Faster and Easier Ways to Diagnose Monkeypox: New Approaches Improve Detection
article.articleSummary: Mpox (monkeypox) diagnosis is shifting from reliance on PCR to scalable point-of-care platforms. After the 2022 WHO Public Health Emergency of International Concern and the 2024 reaffirmation, mpox spread beyond Africa; the 2022 outbreak involved more than 60,000 cases in over 100 countries. Mpox began with a 1970 human case in the Democratic Republic of Congo; reservoirs include primates, rodents, and other small mammals; human infection follows animal bites/scratches or close contact, then fever, lymphadenopathy, and a vesiculo-pustular rash, complicating clinical diagnosis. PCR on skin lesions remains the reference test but is lab-based. Serology is limited by cross-reactivity; rapid antigen tests are quicker but less sensitive. LAMP and RPA offer isothermal alternatives, with CRISPR/LAMP or CRISPR/RPA achieving high sensitivity and potential clade differentiation, yet cost and cold-chain limits persist. Future directions: electrochemical/paper-based sensors, microfluidics, 3D printing, and AI-driven smartphone tools under REASSURED criteria.

article.articleHeadline: Squirrel bites over 18 people at Udaipur university, then vanishes without a trace
article.articleSummary: As of May 1, 2026, a squirrel at Mohanlal Sukhadia University in Udaipur has bitten more than 18 people over the past month, mainly around the Arts College campus near the Psychology and Women's Studies departments. The animal reportedly attacked two research scholars on April 22. Efforts to capture the squirrel by Animal Aid were unsuccessful; wildlife experts are being brought in to relocate it to a safer habitat. The animal's unusual behavior—hiding behind curtains and leaping out to strike—has heightened concerns and disrupted campus life, with some students avoiding areas. Experts note extreme heat could contribute to heightened aggression in small animals, especially after periods of hunger. Injured individuals have received tetanus injections from the Animal Husbandry Department; no capture has occurred yet, but officials are pursuing renewed attempts to regain control.

article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Gresik Regency Government Anticipates Foot-and-Mouth Disease Ahead of Eid al-Adha, Intensifies Vaccination.
article.articleSummary: Foot-and-Mouth Disease (PMK) vaccination program in Gresik Regency, Indonesia, intensified ahead of Eid al-Adha to safeguard sacrificial livestock. The drive centers at Balongpanggang Livestock Market, a key cross-district hub bordering Lamongan and Mojokerto, where livestock trade has surged by up to 100% as traders arrive from Gresik, Mojokerto, Lamongan, Sidoarjo, Probolinggo, and Lumajang. The campaign targets cattle and goats, with vaccination delivered by PMK task forces and Puskeswan, including door-to-door outreach and market vaccination. Buyers are advised to choose vaccinated animals, marked by ear tags with barcodes. Balongpanggang hosts two markets—Kedungpring and Balongpanggang—and local authorities coordinate with Puskeswan, Koramil, and Polsek to ensure safe and orderly trading. The effort underscores ongoing preventive measures and surveillance against FMD during Eid al-Adha.

article.articleHeadline: Should You Wash Chicken Before Cooking? AIIMS-Trained Doctor Warns It Can Spread Bacteria - Woman's era Magazine
article.articleSummary: Salmonella and Campylobacter can be present in raw chicken. AIIMS, New Delhi-trained neurologist Dr. Rahul Chawla warns that washing under running water does not remove these bacteria and instead spreads them through splashes to countertops, utensils, sinks, and nearby foods. The article notes that this cross-contamination risk persists despite common beliefs that rinsing improves hygiene. Health authorities, including the US FDA and CDC, advise against washing raw poultry. Proper cooking to safe internal temperatures remains the only reliable method to kill pathogens, regardless of washing. Safer alternatives include trimming visible impurities and wiping instead of rinsing; if washing is attempted, do so in a bowl to minimize splashes, followed by thorough hand, utensil, and surface cleaning. Emphasizes overall kitchen hygiene: separate cutting boards and sanitizing surfaces to prevent illness.

In a Radio Okapi interview with Blaise Ndongala Mayanda, Mabala urged parents to vaccinate their children to strengthen their immune systems and protect against diseases preventable by vaccination, aligning with polio eradication efforts. He also noted ongoing hospital reforms to improve access to quality care. The report underscores immunization as a key public health measure and highlights continued outreach to families to ensure vaccines are administered according to schedule.

article.articleSummary: As of May 1, 2026, Campinas, Brazil, declares the 18th Arboviroses Alert of 2026, intensifying Aedes aegypti control as the city lists 28 neighborhoods under alert for dengue, Zika, and chikungunya. Authorities emphasize preventing water stagnation and proper waste disposal to curb vector proliferation. The measures build on ongoing interventions, with a warning that favorable weather in coming weeks could sustain transmission. Early identification of new breeding sites and rapid response by teams are critical to limiting new cases in monitored zones.

article.articleHeadline: Dourados tem drive-thru de vacinação contra chikungunya nesta sexta-feira
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Dourados has a drive-through vaccination against chikungunya this Friday.
article.articleSummary: Drive-through chikungunya vaccination planned in Dourados, Mato Grosso do Sul, on Friday, May 1, at the Municipal Administrative Center, 8:00–12:00, targeting adults 18–59 without contraindications. The single-dose vaccine, per Instituto Butantan and Valneva guidelines, requires a five-minute pre-screening; contraindications include pregnancy, lactation, immunosuppression, active cancer treatment, recent transplant, autoimmune diseases, and BMI >30. Dourados faces a severe outbreak, with 9 confirmed chikungunya deaths and 2,755 confirmed plus 5,271 probable cases in the city. MS accounts for 66% of the national 21 chikungunya deaths, with the state total at 14 deaths. Indigenous territories in Dourados report 2,474 probable cases and eight of the nine deaths. Symptoms include high fever and severe joint pain; 35 hospitalized and three deaths under lab investigation. Vaccination also available through regular health units with extended hours at select posts to ease urgent-care pressure.

triage.notes: 記事はブラジルのマット・グロッソ・ド・スル州ドゥアルドス市におけるチクングニア流行への対応を主題としているが、ブラジルは対象国リストに含まれないため verified_locations は空配列とする。ただし、9名死亡、7,026疑い例を含む重篤な流行イベントであり、地域的には重要なシグナルである。

article.articleHeadline: Rolante intensifica ações de prevenção à raiva após casos confirmados e suspeitos
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Rolante intensifies rabies prevention measures after confirmed and suspected cases.
article.articleSummary: On 27 April, in Rolante, Brazil, municipal leaders gathered to align rabies prevention and control measures following confirmed and suspected cases. The meeting, requested by Mayor Alceu Trevizani, included health and agriculture secretaries, the municipal inspection service, and veterinary and epidemiological staff. Officials stressed rabies as a high-urgency zoonosis with no cure and a high fatality risk for humans and animals, underscoring the need for preventive actions. Producers were advised to report potential bat roost locations and to promptly notify authorities of any animal bite incidents; bats remain legally protected, and any control measures must be carried out solely by official agencies. The administration also reinforced annual vaccination campaigns for a wide range of species: cattle, buffalo, horses, pigs, sheep, goats, and both dogs and cats, in urban and rural areas to curb disease spread.

triage.headline_ja: ロランテがラビーズ（狂犬病）の確認例および疑い例に続いて予防措置を強化
triage.triage_reason: ブラジルでの狂犬病の確認例および疑い例の報告であり、地域レベルの予防措置が実施されている。ただし、患者数、重症度、国際的拡大リスクの詳細が不明であるため、現段階ではWATCH判定とし、続報の監視が必要である。
triage.notes: 狂犬病は致死的な疾患であり、人獣共通感染症として重要である。記事では複数の確認例および疑い例が報告されており、市民レベルでの緊急対応（例：市長による召集会議）が実施されている。ただし、確認患者数、入院患者数、死亡例の具体的数字が記事サマリーに含まれていないため、重症度評価は不明とした。追加の流行情報や患者統計が入手可能になれば、PICKUP判定への昇格を検討すべき。

article.articleHeadline: Na pista da BR-319, a fratura na floresta e o prenúncio de novas crises sanitárias
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: On the BR-319 Trail, the Fracture in the Forest and the Omen of New Health Crises.
article.articleSummary: BR-319 paving between Manaus and Porto Velho proceeds after TRF-1 overturned a 70-day suspension of DNIT bids, with relaunch planned. The central Amazon project intensifies forest fragmentation, increasing human–wildlife contact and potential pathogen spillover in a region home to thousands of unknown wildlife viruses. The route would affect 69 Indigenous Lands housing 18 peoples, including groups in voluntary isolation, elevating malaria, leishmaniasis, and dengue risks as ecological changes alter water regimes and create degraded habitats; mining and illegal activity may contaminate water with mercury. The article urges a pre-construction Strategic Health Plan for the BR-319 basin, including regional hospitals (Humaitá, Careiro, Manicoré), trained health professionals, permanent disease surveillance, and border laboratories linked to Fiocruz Amazônia, USP, UFRJ, and Project Orion, plus expanded DSEIs with aeromedical transport. Health safeguards are deemed essential before road completion.

triage.headline_ja: BR-319道路上で：森林の分断と新たな衛生危機の兆候
triage.triage_reason: アマゾンにおける大規模インフラプロジェクトに伴う森林破壊による動物由来感染症（マラリア、リーシュマニア症、デング熱）の急速な蔓延リスクが明記されており、IHR基準4項目中3項目（重大な公衆衛生影響、異常性、国際的拡大リスク）、WPRO基準5項目中4項目（異常性、重症度、長期曝露、流行可能性）が該当。地域検証済み（ブラジル対象国）。
triage.notes: 記事はBR-319高速道路のマナウス～ポルトベーリョ間舗装工事に伴う森林破壊と、それによるマラリア、リーシュマニア症、デング熱などの人獣共通感染症リスク増加について論述。アマゾナス州、ロンドーニア州、パラー州の複数地域が影響を受ける。69の先住民族領土、18の民族（自発的隔離集団を含む）が影響対象。記事はFiocruz Amazônia、USP、UFRJおよびProject Orionとの連携による先制的な戦略的保健計画の必要性を強調。既知外のウイルス数千種を宿す地域での生態系変化に伴う新興感染症リスクも指摘されている。

article.articleHeadline: Bird Flu outbreak in Nandurbar; 1.4 Lakh chickens to be culled
article.articleSummary: Bird flu (avian influenza) outbreak confirmed at poultry farms in Navapur, Nandurbar district, Maharashtra. Samples from three farms tested positive at a laboratory in Indore, prompting immediate culling of about 1.4 lakh chickens across six farms within a one‑kilometre radius. Officials warn up to roughly 10 lakh chickens in the surrounding area could be at risk if the infection spreads. A three‑kilometre containment zone and a five‑kilometre buffer zone are being established, with strict surveillance and biosecurity measures. A taluka‑level monitoring committee has started sampling all poultry farms in Navapur. The district administration will provide financial assistance to affected farm owners after state assessment, and action will be taken against operators negligent in safety protocols. Outbreak reported on May 1, 2026.

triage.headline_ja: ナンドゥルバルで鳥インフルエンザ流行、14万羽の鶏が処分対象
triage.triage_reason: インドでの鳥インフルエンザの確認事例であり、異常・予想外の事象、複数地域への波及リスク、公衆衛生への影響が認められるため、IHR基準およびWPRO基準を複数満たす。
triage.notes: 鳥インフルエンザの確認事例。マハーラシュトラ州およびマディヤプラデシュ州で検査陽性が確認され、大規模な家禽処分（14万羽）が実施される。周囲地域で最大10万羽の追加リスク。3km隔離地帯および5kmバッファゾーン設定。人への感染報告はないが、鳥インフルエンザの人獣共通感染リスクは存在するため監視が必要。

article.articleHeadline: 大摩邇（おおまに） : タイで類鼻疽の感染増加　23人死亡、注意呼びかけ
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Oomani: Increase in anthrax-like infections in Thailand; 23 dead, warning issued.
article.articleSummary: Melioidosis (anthrax-like infection caused by Burkholderia pseudomallei) infections in Thailand surged nationwide, with 732 cases and 23 deaths reported Jan 1–Apr 16, according to the government on Apr 18. The soil- and water-borne bacterium can enter the body via skin wounds, contaminated water, or inhalation, causing acute to chronic illness. Common presentations include pneumonia (fever, cough, dyspnea), skin/soft tissue infections with abscesses, sepsis, and multilocular abscesses in liver, spleen, kidney, or prostate; septic shock can occur. High-risk groups include agricultural workers and people with diabetes, chronic kidney disease, chronic lung disease, or immune suppression. Officials urge protective measures for those touching soil or water (boots, gloves) and prompt medical care for two days of fever, shortness of breath, or suspected wounds; a 24/7 hotline is available (1422). The article notes the disease’s tropical distribution, with travel-related cases reported in Japan as imported infections. Diagnosis relies on culture from blood, sputum, urine, or abscess fluid.

triage.headline_ja: タイで類鼻疽の感染増加　23人死亡、注意呼びかけ
triage.triage_reason: IHR基準3つ以上該当（深刻な公衆衛生影響、異常/予想外な感染増加、国際的拡大リスク）。スクリーニング基準5つ全て該当。シグナル性高く、フルRRA進行が必須。
triage.notes: 記事は主にタイでの類鼻疽（メリオイドーシス）の急速な増加を報じており、732例・23死亡という実質的な公衆衛生危機を示している。農業労働者など高リスク群の特定、政府の公式警告、24/7ホットライン設置など対応体制が機能していることが確認される。日本への渡航関連輸入例の言及もあり、国際的拡大リスクが実在する。土壌・水媒介性細菌感染症で環境要因も重要。

article.articleHeadline: छत्तीसगढ़ की राष्ट्रीय मंच पर दोहरी उपलब्धि, फाइलेरिया व मलेरिया नियंत्रण मॉडल की देशभर में सराहना
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Chhattisgarh's twofold achievement on the national platform: nationwide praise for the lymphatic filariasis and malaria control model.
article.articleSummary: Chhattisgarh was nationally recognized at the National Summit on Innovation and Inclusivity in Chandigarh (April 30–May 1, 2026) for its lymphatic filariasis and malaria elimination model. The BIHAN model, under the State Rural Livelihood Mission, mobilized women’s self-help groups and was named the country’s best innovative and inclusive initiative by the Mission Steering Group-Human Resource, with PCI India providing technical support. During the MDA campaign, women conducted door-to-door drug administration and community meetings to dispel myths, increasing uptake; about 74% of initial refusers consented to treatment. The Malaria-Free Bastar campaign in remote tribal areas used home screening, rapid diagnostic tests, prompt treatment, and Day-7/Day-14 follow-ups to ensure full cure and to identify asymptomatic infections. State API fell from 1.97 to 0.90 (2019–2025), Bastar division API from 13.12 to 6.98. The model is praised as replicable for other states; plans emphasize community-based, innovative, region-specific strategies.

triage.headline_ja: チャッティスガル州の国家的二重成果：全国でリンパ系フィラリア症およびマラリア制御モデルが称賛される
triage.triage_reason: 本記事は疾病制御の成功事例と政策表彰に関するポジティブニュースであり、新規発生や急速な感染拡大を示唆する指標がない。IHR基準および WPRO スクリーニング基準のいずれにも該当しない。
triage.notes: 本記事はマラリアおよびリンパ系フィラリア症の制御成功に関する報告であり、感染症の新規発生・拡大・危機的状況を示唆していない。むしろ疾病負荷の低下（API 1.97→0.90）を報告している。シグナル検出の観点からは見送り対象。

article.articleHeadline: Brain infection claims 26-yr-old woman, health alert in Kerala
article.articleSummary: A 26-year-old nurse in Kerala’s Thiruvananthapuram died from suspected amoebic meningoencephalitis, triggering a health alert for potential new cases. Arya, a resident of Neerkunnam near Ambalapuzha in Alappuzha district, was first admitted in Alappuzha last month with AME symptoms and later moved to Government Medical College Hospital, Thiruvananthapuram, for advanced care. Her condition worsened Thursday night and she died on Friday. The death follows a brief lull in reported cases, with officials warning that prevailing climatic conditions could foster fresh infections. Amoebic meningoencephalitis is caused by Naegleria fowleri and Acanthamoeba—microorganisms found in contaminated water bodies. The report describes the case as suspected, with no lab confirmation provided, and notes the potential for future exposures linked to water sources and climate factors in Kerala as of 1 May 2026.

triage.headline_ja: 脳感染症が26歳女性の命を奪う、ケーラ州で健康警報
triage.triage_reason: ナグレリア fowleri による髄膜脳炎の死亡例報告。予防不可能な水中病原体による重症感染症であり、異常・予想外の発症、重症度（死亡）、長期曝露リスク（環境水源）、流行しやすさ（気候条件による拡大懸念）の複数スクリーニング基準に該当。社会的関心および地域の公衆衛生上の懸念あり。
triage.notes: ナグレリア fowleri は極めて予後不良の水中病原体。本事例は疑い例であるが、ケーラ州における季節的・気候的リスク要因の指摘と新規症例警戒により公衆衛生上の重要性あり。水源汚染との関連性が認識されている点が懸念される。

article.articleHeadline: लैब रिपोर्टः कर्नाटक के तुमकुरु में 'बर्ड फ्लू' की वजह से हुई 44 मोरों की मौत
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Lab report: 44 peacocks died in Tumakuru, Karnataka due to 'bird flu'.
article.articleSummary: Lab report confirms H5N1 avian influenza caused the deaths of 44 peacocks in Tumakuru district, Karnataka. The outbreak first appeared around 16 April; within a week, 44 dead peacocks were found in Tumakuru taluk, notably in Kesaramadu, Hirehalli, and Gulur gram panchayats' fields, after a search. Samples were sent to ICAR-National Institute of High Security Animal Diseases (NIHSAD) in Bhopal, which confirmed H5N1 as the cause. Since 23 April, no new cases in Tumakuru taluk. Authorities, including Forest, Health, and Animal Husbandry departments, are coordinating to curb spread. A 10-km radius around affected areas has been declared a restricted zone, and nearby poultry farms have been alerted to monitor and implement precautions.

triage.headline_ja: ラボ報告：カルナータカ州トゥムクルでの『鳥インフルエンザ』による孔雀44羽の死亡
triage.triage_reason: インド国内における野生動物（孔雀）でのH5N1確認だが、人間への感染報告がなく、現在は新規患者報告がない。IHR基準は1つのみ該当で、WPROスクリーニング基準では異常性と感染拡大可能性が認められるが、ヒト-ヒト感染の証拠がなく、人的影響の評価が不明。継続経過観察が必要。
triage.notes: 本事例は野生動物（孔雀）でのH5N1確認であり、人間への感染報告はない。4月16日頃に発生、4月23日以降新規患者報告なし。カルナータカ州トゥムクル地区での制限区域設定と家禽農場への警戒喚起が実施されている。野生動物でのH5N1は鳥類の国際移動に伴う拡大リスク（バイオセキュリティ）があり、今後の人間への感染可能性を含めた動向監視が必要。

article.articleHeadline: Dinkes Bangka Temukan 9 Kasus Tuberkulosis Anak, Skrining di Sungailiat Diperketat
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Bangka Health Office Finds 9 Pediatric Tuberculosis Cases, Screening in Sungailiat Intensified
article.articleSummary: Nine pediatric tuberculosis cases were identified in Bangka Regency, Kepulauan Bangka Belitung, in 2026, with intensified TB screening in Sungailiat and surrounding areas. The Bangka Health Office (Dinkes) notes active case-finding at local health facilities; pediatric TB can reflect adult-to-child transmission within the close environment. To curb transmission, authorities are expanding Bacillus Calmette-Guerin (BCG) vaccination, targeting 5,108 newborns across the district; as of early May 2026, 797 have received BCG in 60 villages/subdistricts. In parallel, contact tracing aims to screen at least 20 people per confirmed TB case to interrupt transmission chains. Parents are urged to ensure complete basic immunization and to seek care at Puskesmas for suspected TB. The initiative supports regional TB elimination goals by 2030.

triage.headline_ja: バンカ保健局が小児結核9例を発見、スンガイリアットでスクリーニング強化
triage.triage_reason: インドネシアで確認された小児結核クラスター（9例）であり、異常性と長期曝露の可能性がWPRO基準を満たすが、情報不足および限定的な地理的範囲により、フルRRA前の経過観察が適切。
triage.notes: 小児結核クラスターは成人から子どもへの感染を示唆し、接触者追跡と予防接種の強化が進行中。死亡例や重症例に関する情報が不足しており、真の重症度は不明。当該地域は限定的だが、BCG接種目標が5,108人と大規模であることから、広範な感染リスク軽減の意図がうかがえる。

article.articleHeadline: Comprou sardinha contaminada com salmonella? Veja o que fazer
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Did you buy sardines contaminated with Salmonella? Here's what to do.
article.articleSummary: Brazil's health regulator Anvisa on 29 April ordered the recall of a batch of frozen sardines after laboratory tests detected Salmonella. The item, frozen sardines beheaded and eviscerated, batch 1309902244 from JMS Indústria e Comércio de Pescados, was deemed unfit for human consumption. Anvisa suspended sale, distribution and use and directed the removal of any remaining units from the market. Salmonella infection can cause vomiting, fever, abdominal pain and diarrhea, with symptoms typically appearing 6–72 hours after ingestion. No illness counts are reported in the article. The recall is voluntary, with the manufacturer informing Anvisa within 48 hours. Consumers who bought the batch should not eat it and should contact the company's customer service for return or replacement. Prevention tips include proper refrigeration, avoiding cross-contamination, thorough cooking of fish, and sanitizing utensils and surfaces.

triage.headline_ja: サルモネラ菌に汚染されたイワシを購入した場合の対処法
triage.triage_reason: 単一バッチの食品リコール事案であり、患者発生報告なし。IHR基準およびWPRO基準の該当なし。
triage.notes: 記事は単一バッチの食品リコール（サルモネラ検出）を報道するもので、感染症の流行事案ではない。患者発生数はゼロと明記されている。ブラジルは対象国外であるため verified_locations は空配列。規制当局による対応は適切に進行中であり、疾患管理上の懸念はない。

article.articleHeadline: DF monitora casos suspeitos de febre Oropouche após confirmação da doença em Goiás
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Federal District monitors suspected cases of Oropouche fever after confirmation of the disease in Goiás.
article.articleSummary: As of May 1, 2026, Goiás state in Brazil has one laboratory-confirmed case of Oropouche fever, prompting health authorities to monitor suspected cases in the Federal District (Distrito Federal). The Secretaria de Saúde reports no confirmed cases in the Federal District at present, but surveillance continues. Suspected cases are being monitored. Oropouche fever is viral; symptoms include fever, headache, and muscle and joint pains (myalgias and arthralgias). People with symptoms should seek care at a health unit prepared to handle such cases. Prevention focuses on reducing mosquito breeding sites to limit transmission. The article does not specify the transmission source or vectors beyond general measures. No further details on outbreak scope or additional cases are provided.

triage.headline_ja: ゴイアス州でのオロポーシュ熱確認後、連邦直轄地区が疑い患者をモニタリング
triage.triage_reason: ブラジルでのオロポーシュ熱の確認例は異常・予想外だが、現時点で1例の確認のみで国際的拡大リスクは未評価。情報不足のため経過観察段階が適切。
triage.notes: オロポーシュ熱はアルボウイルスによる感染症で、蚊媒介感染が示唆されている。記事では確認例が1例のみであり、重症度や流行規模について詳細情報が不足している。ブラジル国内での公衆衛生当局による監視体制が構築されていることが確認される。続報により症例数の増加やクラスター形成の有無を注視する必要がある。

article.articleHeadline: Indonesia's malaria battle: How a woman helps protect Papua's villages
article.articleSummary: Malaria battle in Papua, Indonesia centers on Siti Ismawati Made, a Kader Perkasa in Kalisusu Village, Nabire District, Central Papua. Since training during COVID-19, she and two colleagues monitor eight neighborhoods, conducting door-to-door checks, urging timely referrals to puskesmas, and emphasizing hygiene to curb transmission. They now handle malaria, TB, and HIV/AIDS. In 2025, Papua's malaria cases exceeded 204,000 across eight districts; Nabire accounted for 8,744 cases, second to Mimika's 190,597. In Jan–Mar 2026, Nabire logged 776 cases. Infants: 790 infections; pregnant women: 108 in 2025. Screening rose 337% from 983,000 tests in 2021 to 4.3 million in 2025. Malaria vectors—female Anopheles—breed in dirty standing water; prevention relies on neat surroundings, mosquito nets, repellents, and examinations. Authorities push cross-sector collaboration and increased diagnosis to accelerate elimination.

triage.headline_ja: インドネシアのマラリア対策：ある女性がパプアの村を守る方法
triage.triage_reason: インドネシア（パプア州）におけるマラリアの深刻な流行。2025年に20万4千例を超え、妊婦・乳幼児を含む多数の重症患者が報告されており、公衆衛生への重大な影響が確認される。スクリーニング基準複数該当（異常性、重症度、長期曝露、流行易感性）。
triage.notes: パプア州（Provinsi Papua）はインドネシア領で、2025年のマラリア症例数が20万4千例を超え、妊婦108例、乳幼児790例を含む。Nabire地区では2026年1-3月に776例が報告されており、継続的な流行が確認される。PNG（パプアニューギニア）も地理的に隣接しているが、記事の主題はインドネシア側の対策であるため、verified_locationsはIndonesiaのみとする。

article.articleHeadline: Penjualan Sapi Kurban di Boyolali Tetap Tinggi meski Ada PMK
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Sacrificial Cattle Sales in Boyolali Remain High Despite Foot-and-Mouth Disease
article.articleSummary: Foot-and-mouth disease (PMK) persists in Boyolali, Central Java, but Idul Adha 2026 sacrificial cattle sales are not deterred. Demand from cattle-producing villages remains strong from H-30 to early May, with buyers from Jabodetabek and West Java. Prices are about 15% higher than the same period last year: cattle around 300 kg at Rp 23 million; Limousin or Simental 400–500 kg at Rp 25–27.5 million; Pattunhan (1/7 share) at Rp 3.3–3.8 million per person; premium cattle 500 kg–1 ton Rp 40–80 million. Veterinary certificates (SKKH) and “surat jalan” are in high demand and widely issued. The Boyolali Disnakkan reports 16,000 PMK vaccine doses allocated for 2026, with 9,424 administered by 29 April 2026. Officials emphasize PMK status has not dampened cattle supply or market activity for Idul Adha.

triage.headline_ja: イドゥル・アドハー期間中、口蹄疫が蔓延するボヨラリでも犠牲家畜の販売が好調
triage.triage_reason: インドネシアで口蹄疫が確認されており異常・予想外な状況ですが、記事の主な焦点は経済活動（家畜販売）であり、公衆衛生への深刻な影響や国際的拡大リスクについては明記されていません。情報不足のため要経過観察とします。
triage.notes: 記事はインドネシアのボヨラリ地域での口蹄疫（PMK）の継続的な存在を報告していますが、焦点は宗教的祭事（イドゥル・アドハー）における家畜販売市場の経済活動にあります。当局は予防接種を実施しており、管理可能性は比較的高いと考えられます。人間への感染リスクについては言及されていません。

article.articleHeadline: Maharashtra bird flu outbreak: Administration on high alert, says commissioner of Animal Husbandry
article.articleSummary: An H5N1 bird flu outbreak has been confirmed in Navapur, Nandurbar district, Maharashtra, after samples from Diamond Poultry Farm tested positive. Local authorities culled about 150,000 chickens and imposed culling within a 1-km radius, with a 3-km containment zone. State Commissioner Dr. Kiran Patil directed actions under the Government of India's Action Plan and called for preventive measures. A District Level Review Committee under the District Collector will finalize strategies, with coordinated efforts across Health, Forest, Water Resources, and local bodies. Forest and Water Departments must monitor reservoirs and wildlife areas; surveillance of poultry blood and reporting of unusual mortality is mandated, with increased zoo monitoring. Under Section 36 of the Prevention and Contagious Diseases in Animals Act, 2009, the district administration has powers to enforce controls. Citizens should report deaths and follow bio-safety protocols and not panic.

triage.headline_ja: マハラシュトラ州鳥インフルエンザ流行：行政が厳戒態勢、動物畜産委員会委員長が声明
triage.triage_reason: インド（マハラシュトラ州ナンドゥルバル地区）でH5N1鳥インフルエンザが確認され、約15万羽の鶏が処分されている。公衆衛生への深刻な影響、国際的な拡大リスク、異常性、管理上の課題が複数該当し、IHR基準を満たす。
triage.notes: H5N1は人獣共通感染症であり、人への感染リスクが存在する。15万羽の大規模処分、複数の監視レイヤー（家禽血液、野生動物、貯水池）の実施、および複数省庁間の調整体制構築は、事態の深刻さを示唆している。WPROスクリーニング基準5項目すべてに該当し、優先度の高いシグナルである。

article.articleHeadline: Replication Efficiency of Contemporary Highly Pathogenic Avian Influenza A(H5N1) Virus Isolates in Human Nasal Epithelium Model
article.articleSummary: Eight influenza A isolates, including contemporary highly pathogenic avian influenza A(H5N1) clade 2.3.4.4b and seasonal strains, were tested in the Mattek EpiNasal human nasal epithelium model to compare replication kinetics and host responses. The HPAI H5N1 A/Texas/37/2024 (B3.13) replicated most efficiently in nasal tissue, surpassing the historical A/Vietnam/1203/2004; the A/mountain lion/MT/1/2024 (B3.6) isolate showed the lowest replication. Mammalian-adaptive PB2 substitutions (E627K, D701N, M631L) correlated with higher replication. ISG responses (ISG15, IFITM3, MX1) were lower for B3.13 than for D1.1 and historical strains despite high replication; proinflammatory cytokines IL-6, TNF-α, and IL-1β were variably induced. Temperature experiments indicated lower early titers at 33°C versus 37°C in MDCK cells, though maximal titers were similar. Overall, contemporary H5N1 may replicate efficiently in the human upper respiratory tract with no demonstrated human-to-human transmission.

triage.headline_ja: 現代的な高病原性鳥インフルエンザA(H5N1)ウイルス分離株のヒト鼻上皮モデルにおける複製効率
triage.triage_reason: H5N1の実験室研究報告であり、ヒト鼻上皮での複製効率を検証したが、実際のヒト-ヒト伝播は示されていない。査読済み学術論文に基づく基礎研究であり、緊急の公衆衛生上の脅威ではないが、H5N1の適応可能性に関する知見として注視すべき。
triage.notes: 本報告は実験室レベルの基礎研究であり、テキサス州とモンタナ州で分離されたH5N1の複製特性を評価したもの。ベトナムは歴史的なH5N1分離株（A/Vietnam/1203/2004）との比較対象として言及されている。実際の疾病発生またはヒト感染事例の報告ではなく、ウイルスの適応傾向を示唆する知見として学術的関心がある。

article.articleHeadline: Indonesia: Estrategias y avances para eliminar la malaria en Papúa - Notiulti
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Indonesia: Strategies and progress to eliminate malaria in Papua - Notiulti.
article.articleSummary: Indonesia has intensified its strategic efforts to eradicate malaria, targeting 2030 as the elimination year through an integrated control system that aims to optimize the national health response. By 2026, the Health Ministry reports 412 malaria-free regions, marking a crucial milestone toward the goal. The Papua region remains a priority, with the TOKEN strategy deployed to curb transmission there and alongside active community participation, with women notably helping to protect Papuan villages from malaria. At the same time, authorities call for closer institutional coordination, urging the Papua Provincial Government to align its malaria programs with central guidelines to ensure actions are consistent with the national health strategy.

triage.headline_ja: インドネシア：パプアにおけるマラリア排除のための戦略と進展
triage.triage_reason: マラリアは対象国インドネシアでの継続的な課題であり、公衆衛生への影響がある。しかし記事サマリーは進展報告が主体で、新規感染症危機やアウトブレイク（異常事象）の報告ではなく、情報不足のため WATCH 段階での経過観察が適切。
triage.notes: 記事はマラリア排除戦略の進展報告であり、新規アウトブレイクや危機的状況の報告ではない。パプア地域での継続的な伝播リスクと政府対応が言及されているが、異常性や予想外性は低い。フルRRA不要だが、インドネシアのマラリア動向の継続監視は推奨される。

article.articleHeadline: Tumakuru Bird Flu Alert: H5N1 Confirmed in Peacock Deaths, Authorities Issue Advisory
article.articleSummary: H5N1 avian influenza confirmed in the deaths of peacocks in Tumakuru district, Karnataka. Peacocks found dead in Kolihalli village, Urdigere taluk; tissue samples were sent to the National Institute of High Security Animal Diseases in Bhopal for analysis, with laboratory results confirming H5N1. Authorities have placed Kolihalli and surrounding areas under strict surveillance and are closely monitoring poultry farms to prevent further spread. Following directions from the Central Government, a high alert was issued to the state Chief Secretary and the District Collector, and a public advisory urged residents not to touch dead birds and to report any unusual bird deaths immediately. Officials said there is no immediate threat to domestic animals and no culling is planned; the situation remains under control with ongoing monitoring.

triage.headline_ja: トゥマクル鳥インフルエンザ警報：H5N1がクジャク死亡で確認、当局が警告を発令
triage.triage_reason: インド（対象国）でH5N1が野生動物（クジャク）で確認されており、異常性と流行性があるシグナルとして該当するが、現在のところ家畜や人への直接的な脅威は報告されておらず、公式な社会的・政治的関心の高さが明示されていない情報段階のため、続報監視が必要。
triage.notes: H5N1は野生動物（クジャク）での検出であり、現在のところ家畜や人への直接的脅威は報告されていない。ただし、H5N1の人獣共通感染の可能性と流行ポテンシャルからWPRO基準で2つのシグナルに該当。当局が中央政府の指示に基づき高度警戒態勢を敷いており、政府レベルの関心がある。情報不足部分（死亡数の規模、地理的拡大状況）が複数あるため、WATCH段階として続報を注視する判定とした。

article.articleHeadline: Influenza: vírus segue forte no país e fica três vezes acima do histórico
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Influenza: the virus remains strong in the country and is three times higher than historical levels.
article.articleSummary: Influenza remains widely circulating in Brazil with elevated transmission. Data from the Brazilian Association of Diagnostic Medicine (Abramed), which covers laboratories responsible for about 85% of outpatient testing, show influenza positivity at 27.3% in early April, down from a recent peak of 31.2% but still three times higher than the 2025 same period (8.09%). The five-week moving average rose from 17.5% to 26.4%, indicating sustained, above-seasonal activity and transmission intensity. Experts attribute part of the pattern to earlier circulation of Influenza A, simultaneous regional spread, and vaccination campaigns still in early stages. The report underscores vaccination for priority groups, vigilant symptom monitoring, and seeking medical evaluation when indicated to relieve healthcare facilities. Data are compiled via METRICARE by Controllab and transmitted to Brazil’s RNDS/DATASUS for national epidemiological surveillance.

triage.headline_ja: インフルエンザ：ウイルスはブラジル全土で依然として強力で、過去の水準の3倍以上となっている
triage.triage_reason: インフルエンザA型の継続的な流行を示す具体的な疫学データ（陽性率27.3%、過去水準の3倍）があり、WPRO基準で異常性・重症度の可能性が認められるが、国際的な拡大リスク、渡航・貿易制限リスクについて明示的な情報がなく、現段階では追加情報の収集が必要。
triage.notes: 記事は季節外の高い陽性率（27.3%、過去水準の3倍）と継続的な伝播を示唆しているが、死亡率や重症例数に関する具体的データが記載されていない。予防接種キャンペーンが進行中であり、保健医療システムは対応可能と思われるが、流行継続の長期見通しは不明確。引き続き疫学データの推移を注視する必要がある。

article.articleHeadline: Sala de espera se transforma em espaço de educação e prevenção da Doença de Chagas em Onça de Pitangui
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Waiting room becomes a space for education and prevention of Chagas disease in Onça de Pitangui.
article.articleSummary: Onça de Pitangui's health unit in Minas Gerais, Brazil, has converted its waiting room into an educational space focused on Chagas disease. Recognizing that the pre-appointment period offers a productive moment to inform patients about public health risks in Brazil, the initiative delivers information on Doença de Chagas, caused by Trypanosoma cruzi and primarily transmitted by the triatomine bug (barbeiro). In a region where Chagas remains a relevant health issue, preventive and educational actions are essential to reduce incidence. By integrating educational content into the reception area, the service extends beyond clinical care to empower individuals, families, and the surrounding community with knowledge on risk identification, symptom recognition, and everyday preventive measures. This effort underscores education as a tool for protection and strengthened public health engagement.

triage.headline_ja: ピタンギ・オンサの待合室がシャーガス病の教育と予防スペースに変身
triage.triage_reason: シャーガス病の教育・予防キャンペーン記事であり、新規の患者発生事例や異常な流行状況を報告していない。公衆衛生への深刻な影響や異常性が認められない。
triage.notes: 本記事はシャーガス病に関する予防教育イニシアティブの報道であり、新規患者発生・流行状況の報告ではない。既知の地域課題に対する公衆衛生対応の取組みを扱っており、シグナル検出の対象外。

article.articleHeadline: "Mồi ngon" của loạt dịch bệnh nguy hiểm: Chuyên gia khuyến cáo phụ huynh làm điều này sớm
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: The "tasty bait" of a series of dangerous diseases: Experts advise parents to do this early.
article.articleSummary: Vietnam reports concurrent rises in meningococcal disease, dengue, and hand, foot, and mouth disease (HFMD) from January–mid-April 2026, raising concerns of a ‘dual/overlapping’ outbreak, especially in the south. Meningococcal disease records 26 cases with 5 deaths (nearly 50% higher than 2025’s 14), predominantly affecting children under 15 (about 46%). Rapid progression can occur within 24 hours, with early flu-like symptoms, and signs such as neck stiffness, photophobia, altered consciousness, seizures, and non-blanching skin rashes. Dengue fever tallies reach 31,927 cases and 4 deaths nationwide, with early spikes in southern provinces; risk rising in the monsoon season due to heat, humidity, water storage, and urban density. HFMD shows ~26,000 cases and 8 deaths, mainly in daycare-aged children; March 2026 saw higher weekly incidence. Prevention emphasizes hygiene, vector control, vaccination (dengue, meningococcal vaccines; HFMD vaccine approved by MOH), timely medical care for fever and neurologic symptoms.

triage.headline_ja: 危険な一連の感染症の「おいしい餌」：専門家は保護者に早期の対策を勧告
triage.triage_reason: ベトナムで髄膜炎菌病、デング熱、手足口病の複数の疾患が同時多発しており、死亡を含む重症例が報告されている。複数のIHR基準に該当し、特に子どもへの影響が顕著であるため、シグナルとしてピックアップが必要。
triage.notes: ベトナムで2026年1月～4月中旬に髄膜炎菌病（26例、死亡5例）、デング熱（31,927例、死亡4例）、手足口病（約26,000例、死亡8例）の複数疾患が同時に増加している。特に髄膜炎菌病は2025年比で約50%増加し、15歳以下の子どもが約46%を占める。WPROスクリーニング基準5つすべてに該当し、複合的な流行対応が必要な段階。

article.articleHeadline: Aquíferos despencando, sumidouros de carbono saturando e dengue avançando para novas latitudes: relatório com 70 pesquisadores e mais de 150 especialistas alerta que clima e biodiversidade entraram em um ciclo de destruição mútua que ameaça energia, água, saúde e trabalho em escala global
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Aquifers Plunging, Carbon Sinks Saturating, and Dengue Advancing to New Latitudes: A Report by 70 Researchers and More Than 150 Specialists Warns That Climate and Biodiversity Have Entered a Cycle of Mutual Destruction That Threatens Energy, Water, Health, and Jobs Worldwide.
article.articleSummary: Dengue is advancing to new latitudes as climate change and biodiversity loss form a systemic crisis, according to the Ten New Insights in Climate Science 2025/2026 report (Cambridge University Press, February 2026). Created by 70 researchers with contributions from over 150 specialists across continents, the analysis covers work published January 2024–June 2025. The report links record heat in 2023–2024 with an expanding ocean heat content and an energy imbalance that keeps warming, even if emissions drop. Terrestrial carbon sinks show stress: Northern Hemisphere biomass declined after 2016; the Amazon rainforest became a net carbon source in 2023; boreal forests in Siberia and Canada face intensified fires. Climate–biodiversity feedbacks amplify each other, reducing carbon uptake and increasing fire and drought risks, worsening dengue spread and threatening energy, water, health, and jobs worldwide. Paris Agreement pledges (NDCs) rely on sinks that may be less reliable.

triage.headline_ja: 水面下降、炭素吸収源飽和、そしてデング熱が新しい緯度に進行：70人の研究者と150人以上の専門家による報告書が、気候と生物多様性が相互破壊のサイクルに入り、エネルギー、水、健康、雇用を世界規模で脅かしていることを警告
triage.triage_reason: デング熱の地理的拡大と気候変動との関連性について学術報告を引用しているが、具体的な現在の流行データ、症例数、死亡数、または明確な国内対応の必要性が記述されていない。環境・気候分析中心であり、感染症イベントの詳細情報が不足している。
triage.notes: 本記事はブラジルのメディアソース由来だが、記事サマリーはデング熱の潜在的な地理的拡大について学術的・推測的に論じており、具体的な流行イベントの詳細（症例数、死亡数、流行地域の明確化）がない。Bluedot APIが示す発生地域（ブラジル、ロシア連邦、カナダ）は、主に気候変動による環境変化の影響地として言及されているものであり、デング流行の実際の発生地を示していない。対象国リストに含まれるのはブラジルのみだが、記事サマリーではブラジルでの具体的なデング流行に言及していない。したがって verified_locations は空配列。気候科学の学術報告であり、現在進行中の明確な感染症危機イベントではないため WATCH 判定とした。

article.articleHeadline: Caso de raiva em morcego é confirmado em Cacoal, RO
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Rabies case in a bat confirmed in Cacoal, Rondônia
article.articleSummary: Rabies case in a bat confirmed in Cacoal, Rondônia, Brazil. The animal was found on the Federal Institute of Rondônia campus (Ifro) and showed atypical behavior, including difficulty flying. Some students contacted the bat; one student was scratched but reported fine. The specimen was captured and sent to Laboratório Central de Saúde Pública de Rondônia (Lacen) in Porto Velho; the rabies diagnosis was disclosed in March. The virus continues circulating in the municipality. In recent years, infected animals have occurred in both urban and rural areas of Cacoal. Veterinarian Christian Silva warned against handling wildlife and noted that post-exposure prophylaxis with vaccine and serum is effective when given promptly. Day-active bats with impaired movement or abnormal behavior are considered suspicious. A regional disease block will be implemented, including vaccinating dogs and cats within a 12-km radius. Health teams have visited Ifro to educate students and staff about rabies risks.

triage.headline_ja: ブラジル・ロンドニア州カコアルでコウモリの狂犬病確認
triage.triage_reason: 動物での狂犬病確認事例であるが、ヒトへの直接的な深刻な影響は限定的（接触学生は症状なし）。ただし地域的なウイルス循環が続いており、公衆衛生上の関心が必要。

article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Karnataka: 44 peacocks die, H5N1 confirmed, containment zone declared in a 10-km radius.
article.articleSummary: H5N1 avian influenza has been confirmed in Tumakuru district, Karnataka, after the deaths of 44 peafowl. Lab results from ICAR-NIHSAD, Bhopal, confirmed H5N1. The mortality occurred after initial sightings on April 16, with 44 birds dying within a week in farms across Kasaramadu, Hirehalli, and Gulur Gram Panchayats. Since April 23, no new deaths have been reported. Wildlife, health, and animal-husbandry departments are coordinating to contain the outbreak. A 10-kilometer containment zone has been declared around the affected area. Poultry farms in the zone are alerted and under surveillance, hospitals are asked to monitor cases, and stocks of PPE kits, masks, medicines, and testing materials have been secured. Authorities continue to monitor the situation and take all necessary steps to prevent spread.

triage.notes: H5N1鳥インフルエンザはパンデミック可能性が高い病原体。動物での確認後の人への感染リスク監視が重要。カルナタカ州タムクル地区での確認で、インドの鳥インフルエンザサーベイランス強化が必要。

article.articleHeadline: Как болезни животных переходят к людям // Видео НТВ
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: How Animal Diseases Are Transmitted to Humans // NTV Video
article.articleSummary: New virus in seafood detected by Chinese scientists. Dozens of people went blind after eating raw fish and shrimp; the pathogen was previously believed not to threaten humans, but it apparently mutated and can now cause severe vision loss. Over the past 50 years, the number of diseases transmitted from animals to humans has risen about fourfold. The piece provides an explanatory look at what other infections, beyond rabies and plague, wild and domestic animals can transmit to people. It highlights growing concerns about zoonotic and foodborne threats and the need for vigilance in seafood safety and monitoring of animal–human disease interfaces. Published May 1, 2026, the video cites Chinese researchers and frames the broader trend of increasing animal-to-human transmission.

article.articleHeadline: Casos de caxumba aumentam cerca de 50% no Rio e autoridades reforçam a importância da vacinação; saiba como se imunizar
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Mumps cases rise by about 50% in Rio de Janeiro, and authorities reiterate the importance of vaccination; learn how to get vaccinated.
article.articleSummary: As of May 1, 2026, Rio de Janeiro state is experiencing a roughly 50% increase in mumps cases, with authorities attributing the surge to missed routine vaccinations. The disease remains active and vaccines are available at health posts. Protection is provided by the measles-mumps-rubella (MMR) vaccine; the first dose is given at 12 months, with a second dose at 15 months as the tetraviral vaccine (measles, mumps, rubella and varicella). State vaccination coverage stands at 85.62% for dose 1 and 70.03% for dose 2. Priority municipalities include Duque de Caxias, Nova Iguaçu, São Gonçalo, and Belford Roxo. The Ministry of Health aims to vaccinate 95% of the target population. Public health messaging emphasizes vaccination as the primary prevention strategy against mumps.

triage.headline_ja: リオデジャネイロの流行性耳下腺炎（おたふく風邪）症例が約50％増加し、当局がワクチン接種の重要性を強調；ワクチン接種方法を知る
triage.triage_reason: ブラジル（リオデジャネイロ州）で流行性耳下腺炎の症例が50％増加し、複数自治体に影響が及んでいる。ワクチン接種率が目標値（95％）を下回る（第1回85.62％、第2回70.03％）状況において、異常・予想外の発症増加であり、継続的な曝露と管理可能性の問題を示唆している。
triage.notes: 記事サマリーに基づき、イベントはブラジルのリオデジャネイロ州で発生している。複数の疾患（麻疹、流行性耳下腺炎、風疹、水痘）が記載されているが、主要な懸念はムンプス（流行性耳下腺炎）の50％増加である。ワクチン接種率が目標を下回ることが増加の原因とされており、公衆衛生当局が対応中である。

article.articleHeadline: Cuiabá tem 'alto risco' para casos de síndrome respiratória, diz Fiocruz | Diario de Cuiabá
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Cuiabá is at 'high risk' for respiratory syndrome cases, says Fiocruz | Diario de Cuiabá
article.articleSummary: As of May 1, 2026, Cuiabá, Mato Grosso, Brazil ranks among 13 of 27 capitals in alert, risk, or high risk for Severe Acute Respiratory Syndrome (SARI) per Fiocruz’s InfoGripe bulletin. Over the past six weeks, SARI activity has risen nationwide, driven by seasonal RSV and influenza A. RSV remains a leading cause of bronchiolitis in children under two. Vaccination is emphasized as the main protection against severe RSV and influenza; the RSV vaccine can be given year-round and is advised for pregnant women from 28 weeks gestation to protect newborns. For influenza-associated SARI, increases are noted in the Central-South and parts of the North/Northeast, while declines occur in Amazonas, Amapá, Pará, Tocantins, Bahia, Ceará, Maranhão, Piauí, Rio Grande do Norte, and Mato Grosso. Goiás, Maranhão, and Tocantins show stabilization. Of 27 capitals, 13 had laboratory-confirmed positives: 852 (43.5%) positive, 880 (44.9%) negative, 50 (2.6%) pending. Among positives, influenza A dominated at 39.1%, followed by SARS-CoV-2 (27.9%), rhinovirus (22.2%), RSV (5.8%), and influenza B (3.2%).

article.articleHeadline: Estudo aponta ação de planta medicinal contra vírus da Covid-19
article.articleHeadlineTranslated: Study points to action of a medicinal plant against the SARS-CoV-2 virus.
article.articleSummary: Galloylquinic acids derived from leaves of Copaifera lucens Dwyer (red copaiba) show multivalent antiviral activity against SARS-CoV-2, the agent of COVID-19. The Brazilian tree is endemic to the Atlantic Forest. In an international study led by Jairo Kenupp Bastos of USP Ribeirão Preto, fractions rich in galloylquinic acids inhibited SARS-CoV-2 in vitro, reducing plaque formation and suppressing viral protein expression. Mechanistic analyses indicated interference with key viral targets: Spike receptor-binding domain, the papain-like protease (PLpro), and the RNA-dependent RNA polymerase, thereby blocking viral entry, replication, and protein production. Anti-inflammatory and immunomodulatory effects may aid host response in severe cases. The multi-target action potentially lowers resistance risk versus single-target antivirals. While promising, steps remain for in vivo and clinical trials; the work underscores Brazil's biodiversity as a source for novel therapeutics, published in Scientific Reports and supported by FAPESP.

article.articleHeadline: Delhi Govt. to declare Leprosy a notifiable disease under the Delhi Epidemic Diseases Act
article.articleSummary: Leprosy will be declared a notifiable disease under the Delhi Epidemic Diseases Act, with the Delhi Health Department submitting the proposal for approval. The notification would require all government and private healthcare providers—clinics, hospitals, and individual practitioners—to report every new leprosy case to the District Leprosy Officer, enabling surveillance, early diagnosis, and prompt treatment with standard MDT available free in government facilities. Delhi joins Tamil Nadu, Maharashtra, Karnataka, and West Bengal in mandatorily notifying leprosy. India still accounts for about 59% of global annual new leprosy cases despite national elimination in 2005; roughly 44.1% of cases are managed by private facilities and go unreported to the NLEP. Benefits include enhanced surveillance, contact tracing and post-exposure prophylaxis, reduced transmission and stigma, better treatment adherence, and progress toward a 2030 transmission-interruption goal. The move aligns with GNCTD Act 1991, with reporting formats to be shared across health institutions.
